display.title: Tanya Shiur 43 (Conclusion): Hashem's Joy in Our Mitzvos, End of Tanya Chapter 33
display.summary_short: The second half of a Yiddish Tanya shiur on chapter 33: the double joy of mitzvos, transforming the yetzer hara, nature as hidden miracles, and the joy of Lag BaOmer.
display.summary_long: This recording is the closing half hour of shiur 43 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, on the end of chapter 33; it begins in the middle of a thought. A Jew's joy is double: he rejoices that Hashem dwells with him, and Hashem rejoices in the mitzvos done in this physical world; the Tzemach Tzedek would give his whole Olam Haba for one pair of tzitzis. Turning darkness into light gives Hashem special pleasure, and Rabbi Goldstein contrasts restraining the yetzer hara each day with transforming it, recalling how the Rebbe Rashab's talks were first brought to the Frierdiker Rebbe. He explains that the kelipos hide G-dliness until the end of galus, that nature is really a chain of miracles we have grown used to, and that light drawn out of the Diaspora's darkness, as in the Frierdiker Rebbe's call to make America a place of Torah, brings the greatest joy. He ends with 'Yismach Yisroel b'osav', one of the Rebbe's Twelve Pesukim, and the joy of Lag BaOmer that week.
display.lesson: Every physical mitzvah gives Hashem great joy, so a Jew should share in that joy and turn the darkness around him into light.

study_text.note: End of chapter 33 only; excerpt of the full shiur 43 recording.

date.note: 'This week is Lag BaOmer, on Thursday'. Lag BaOmer fell on Thursday in 5738 (also 5745, 5748); 5738 best fits the series.
